historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle volume growth (Onslow 40Mtpa, Mining Services contract growth, Mt Marion +100kt SC6) after a Y1 reset from FY26 peak pricing and the POSCO deconsolidation; equity 5yr CAGR (6.3%) not used because FY26 equity embeds peak lithium earnings and the FY22-25 equity path was flat through a $3bn debt-funded build
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.3% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 11.6% (>30% divergence): revenue growth was debt-funded (net debt 1.3bn FY21 -> 5.3bn FY25) and half the period's earnings went to dividends/impairments. EPS CAGRs are meaningless across a FY25 loss (-4.59) and FY21 peak (6.73).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY21 529, FY22 -743, FY23 -539, FY24 -2,776, FY25 -2,728, FY26 711. The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR of 6.1% is endpoint-driven and hides four consecutive years of negative FCF during the Onslow build; 3yr is undefined (negative start). Reported and owner FCF diverge by only ~150/yr -- SBC is ~1% of revenue, an SBC-light market.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle reset from a record FY26. Base FY27 revenue ~6,070 (-6%) and Underlying EBITDA ~2,250 as SC6 spodumene settles around US$1,400/t and POSCO takes 30% of the Wodgina/Mt Marion share (proceeds A$1,079m in the bridge), while Onslow lifts to 40Mtpa and Mining Services grows from its 976 record. Group margin settles at 36% -- above the FY22-26 average because the Onslow build is complete and Lamb Creek replaces higher-cost Wonmunna. FY27 capex at the ~$1.4bn guided level, then sustaining-plus ~13.5% of revenue. Cash tax ramps from ~10% (FY25 losses) to 30%, with MSIP's 49% of the haul-road trust charged as a ~10pp leakage on EBIT. The axes are lithium and iron ore price, Onslow volume and unit cost, and whether growth capex keeps clearing the 20% post-tax hurdle.
scenario_narratives.bull: All three engines fire together: lithium deficit holds SC6 near US$2,000/t, iron ore stays ~US$100/dmt, Onslow beats 40Mtpa and Mining Services approaches $1.2bn EBITDA. Margins hold ~38%, revenue grows 3-5% despite POSCO, leverage falls below 1x and buybacks/dividends resume at scale. Governance overhang fades with the ASIC close-out and a clean succession.
scenario_narratives.bear: A repeat of FY24-25 pricing: lithium back below US$1,000/t and iron ore US$75-80/dmt. Revenue falls ~20% over two years, margin compresses to 28-30%, FY27 capex is committed, and the tax shelter is used slowly. Net debt drifts back above 2x and the dividend is suspended. The class action and Ellison succession add a discount. Terminal capped at 12x FCF.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value MinRes through the cycle, not at the FY26 peak. Mining Services is a genuinely contracted, growing annuity worth a full multiple; iron ore and lithium are priced at mid-cycle with the FY26 lithium windfall explicitly not extrapolated. The POSCO sale and the Onslow carry loan are balance-sheet events carried in the bridge with their income removed from the flows. MSIP's 49% of the haul road is charged as a leakage on EBIT so the NCI is paid for exactly once. The result is deliberately well below a peak-multiple valuation; the current price sits between the base and bull cases and requires FY26-like commodity prices to persist.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lithium price path: every US$500/t on SC6 is roughly A$300-350m of pre-POSCO EBITDA (about A$1.0-1.2/share of value at the mid-cycle multiple)
Iron ore price and Onslow product discount: Onslow is ~58% Fe and sells at a discount to Platts 62% that widens when Chinese mills chase quality
POSCO completion risk (conditions precedent, H1 FY27): if it fails, remove A$1,079m from the bridge and restore 30% of Wodgina/Mt Marion flows
Capex discipline: FY27 ~$1.4bn is guided; the model assumes it tapers to sustaining-plus by Y4. A new large growth project (international expansion, Energy) would push FCF out again
Combined tax/NCI leakage assumed 40% mature; if the haul-road trust NCI share grows faster than group EBIT the leakage is understated
Governance: shareholder class action (Victorian Supreme Court) unquantified; Ellison succession without a fixed date
FX: US$3bn+ of USD bonds against AUD reporting; a weaker AUD lifts net debt in AUD terms but also lifts AUD-realised commodity prices

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average for diluted EPS, FY26 annual report note (198,793,131); shares on issue ~199m. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it.
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings 332 current + 5,497 non-current = 5,829 (FY26 AR note 19) less cash 1,562 = 4,267, which ties to the company's own reported net debt. EXCLUDES lease liabilities (141) under lease treatment (B). Iron-ore prepayment facility (US$300m) was repaid from the April-2026 notes and is nil at balance date.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY26 OCF 2,084 less investing capex 1,222 (PP&E 734 + intangibles 9 + exploration 29 + mine development 450). OCF is flattered by 430 of Onslow carry-loan repayments from JV partners and depressed by 608 of iron-ore prepayment repayments; the forward build is from EBITDA components so neither distortion carries forward.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 annual report cash-flow reconciliation, 'Share-based payments 77' (FY25: 22). No net-share-settlement tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 across history).
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income 74 (FY26 IS), which includes BBSW+2.9% interest on the Onslow carry loan. Stripped from the base because cash and the carry-loan receivable are both carried in the bridge; leaving the income in the flows would count them twice.
inputs.buyback_note: No buybacks since FY23 (2.8m). The flat share count is a modelling convention, not a funded program; dividends were reinstated FY26 at $0.83/share (20% of Underlying NPAT).
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: AU 10yr ~4.4% + beta ~1.3 x ERP 5.5% = CoE ~11.5%; pre-tax cost of debt 7.4% (weighted average after the April-2026 refinancing, 6.9% post-POSCO redemption) = ~5.2% after 30% tax; D/(D+E) ~28% at market (net debt 4.3bn vs equity 10.9bn) gives ~9.7%, rounded to 10.0%. One WACC across all scenarios; cyclicality, lithium/iron-ore price risk and governance risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: 'Payment of lease liabilities and asset financing arrangements' 198 (FY26 financing) plus lease interest (~10) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path ~3.0% of revenue; lease liabilities (141) EXCLUDED from net debt. Underlying EBITDA 2,551 is post-IFRS-16 so the charge is not already in the margin. D&A 928 includes right-of-use depreciation; tax EBIT is taken after the lease charge with da_pct held at 14%, which slightly overstates D&A ex-ROU and therefore slightly understates cash tax -- immaterial at the 40% combined rate.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows via the cash_tax_rate_path. MSIP owns 49% of the Onslow Iron Road Trust (haul road); NCI profit FY26 154, cash distributions to unitholder 124. The trust's income is untaxed at trust level, so MinRes' NOPAT = (EBIT - NCI) x 0.7. With NCI ~150-170 against mid-cycle EBIT ~1,150-1,250 that is a ~10pp leakage, so the mature combined rate is 30% statutory + ~10pp = 40%. The NCI book value (473) is NOT deducted in the bridge (charging it once).
inputs.cash_tax_note: FY26 cash tax was a 5 refund against a 387 P&L charge (deferred); FY25 loss and accelerated Onslow deductions shelter roughly one year of mid-cycle taxable income. Path: Y1 10% + 10pp NCI = 20%, Y2 25% + 10 = 35%, Y3+ 30% + 10 = 40%.
inputs.posco_and_carry_loan: POSCO Holdings pays ~US$765m for 30% of MinRes' share of Wodgina and Mt Marion (MinRes 50% -> 35% of each); agreements executed 1 May 2026, completion expected H1 FY27 subject to conditions precedent. Treated as a BALANCE-SHEET event: +A$1,079m in equity_bridge (US$765m / AUDUSD 0.7089, Yahoo AUDUSD=X 2026-09-23) and the attributable lithium revenue/EBITDA in the flows reduced by 30% of the Wodgina/Mt Marion share from Y1 (Bald Hill 100% untouched). Onslow carry-loan receivable A$335m (FY26 AR note 11, down from 745) added to the bridge; its repayments run through OCF historically but are excluded from the component build.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the cyclical adaptations (references/owner-fcf-adaptations.md). MIN is a diversified miner (iron ore ~56% of FY26 revenue, lithium ~20%) plus a contracted Mining Services business (~24% external revenue, ~38% of Underlying EBITDA; >85% life-of-mine contracts) -- an operating company whose value is a cash-flow stream, so the owner-FCF engine applies; no REIT/bank/LIC characteristics. THROUGH-CYCLE BUILD, not FY26 extrapolation: FY26 was a record (Underlying EBITDA 2,551, 39.5% margin) on H2 lithium prices around US$2,000-2,400/t SC6 (lithium EBITDA 771, of which 604 in H2) and Platts 62% ~US$100-108/dmt. Base case resets Y1 to mid-cycle: SC6 ~US$1,400/t (lithium EBITDA ~650 pre-POSCO, ~480 post), iron ore ~US$85/dmt offset by Onslow 35->40Mtpa and Lamb Creek replacing Wonmunna (iron ore EBITDA ~1,000), Mining Services ~1,050 (FY27 guided to grow from 976), Energy/central ~-200: ~2,330 on ~6,070 revenue = ~37%, easing to 36%. Historical Underlying EBITDA margins: FY22 31%, FY23 37%, FY24 20%, FY25 20%, FY26 39.5% -- the 36% mature margin sits above the raw 5yr average because FY24-25 were the Onslow construction/ramp years with a lithium trough. Capex: FY27 guidance ~$1.4bn (23% of Y1 revenue), tapering to ~13.5% (FY26 sustaining 643 incl 300 deferred stripping + exploration 60 = ~11% of revenue, plus modest brownfield growth). Terminal cap 14x FCF (cyclical band 12-15x; upper-mid because ~40% of EBITDA is long-dated contracted services and both MSIP (haul road) and POSCO (lithium) have paid ~6x EBITDA for minority stakes). Statutory EBITDA in the CSV (3,003) includes ~450 of one-off gains (Lucky Bay, Onslow Iron Road Trust contingent payment 134, FX); Underlying 2,551 is the anchor.

bear.narrative: Lithium reverses to US$800-1,000/t as 2024-25 showed it can; Chinese steel demand pushes Platts 62% to US$75-80/dmt; Onslow stalls at 35Mtpa with lower-grade discounts widening. Margin 28-30% (still above the FY24-25 construction-year 20% because Onslow is built). FY27 capex commitments cannot be cut. Class action and founder-succession overhang persist; dividend suspended again. TV capped at 12x.

base.narrative: Y1 revenue -6%: POSCO removes 30% of Wodgina/Mt Marion attributable sales and SC6 normalises from ~US$2,000+ to ~US$1,400/t, partly offset by Onslow 35->40Mtpa and Bald Hill's first full year. Margin 37% -> 36% mid-cycle. FY27 capex per guidance ~$1.4bn then tapering to sustaining-plus. Combined tax/NCI rate 20% -> 40% as FY25 losses are used. wc_capture -8%: receivables + inventory > payables for a miner, so growth consumes cash.

bull.narrative: Lithium market moves into deficit late 2026 and SC6 holds ~US$2,000/t; iron ore stays ~US$100/dmt; Onslow exceeds 40Mtpa with the 6th/7th transhippers; Mining Services reaches $1.2bn EBITDA. Revenue grows despite the POSCO deconsolidation; margin ~38% sustained. Tax shelter used faster.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 30%: two of three segments are direct commodity-price takers, lithium has already collapsed once this cycle (management admitted misjudging it), net debt is still $4.3bn, a shareholder class action is live and founder succession is unresolved. Bull cut to 20% because it needs lithium AND iron ore to stay elevated simultaneously while Onslow exceeds nameplate. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
